panels.title: What this board is, and what each number's instrument is

options.content:
Every panel names the process it was measured **in**, because M5 measured the same quantities from the client side and the two are not the same number.

* **Predictor-side** panels come from mlserver's own `/metrics` on port **8082** (probed, not assumed — KServe's own pod annotation advertises 8080, which 404s on this runtime). They exclude the network and the ingress hop, so they will read *lower* than `make load`'s p95 (M5-S4: p50 17.2 / p95 104.2 ms at 4 req/s, concurrency 8 — the client's number, and the one the SLO document owns).
* **Edge** panels come from ingress-nginx and include that hop. They are also the only place a request that never reached the pod appears at all.
* **Container** panels come from the kubelet's cAdvisor. `nr_throttled` is here because a load test run at the CPU limit measures the quota rather than the service (gotcha #74), and that shows up as latency, never as an error.

No threshold is drawn on this board. Thresholds are the SLO document's (M6-S2), and a bar drawn here would be a bar set from the number just observed.

panels.title: Predictor · request rate by status code (mlserver :8082)
panels.description: The 5xx/422 split the SLO document separates: a 5xx is ours, a 422 is the request's (F-019's typed refusal past the holiday horizon, and F-030's NaN body before it was fixed).

panels.title: Predictor · inference latency p50/p95/p99 (server-side)
panels.description: histogram_quantile over mlserver's own duration histogram. Server-side: it does not include the ingress hop or the client's queueing, which is why the SLO's p95 target names the load shape it holds at.

panels.title: Model · successful vs failed inferences, by InferenceService
panels.description: Broken out by isvc so the shadow (M6-S3) and canary (M6-S4) services appear here the moment they exist — the scrape job discovers them by label, not by name.

panels.title: Edge · requests through ingress-nginx by status (per host)
panels.description: The only instrument that sees a request which never reached a pod — a 502/503 during a pod loss, and (from M6-S4) the per-backend split a canary weight actually produced, as opposed to the weight that was asked for.

panels.title: Container · CPU cores used vs the 2-core limit
panels.description: M5-S4 measured 1.31 mean cores at 4 req/s against a request of 200m — the ~6x understatement M6-S2 re-sizes. The limit line is the ceiling the next panel says whether we are hitting.

panels.title: Container · CFS throttling (nr_throttled), and pod restarts
panels.description: Two signals that do not show up as errors. Throttling is what saturation looks like (gotcha #74); a restart count that moves without a deploy is A-5's whole point.
